name: Border Roads Organisation
summary: The army-led road builders who make and keep open the highest, coldest and most remote roads in India.
ownership: Government of India — Ministry of Defence
about: BRO was raised in May 1960 to build roads to India's frontiers, and it has been doing the country's hardest road work ever since. Its crews work at altitudes where engines lose power and concrete struggles to set, clearing snow off passes every spring so that Ladakh and the high Himalaya can be reached by road at all. Alongside the roads it builds bridges, airfields and tunnels, and it works in friendly neighbouring countries too. Much of what BRO builds is eventually handed over to NHAI or a state PWD to run day to day.
facts: Raised on 7 May 1960, and works under the Ministry of Defence rather than the highways ministry.
Built and maintains the Manali–Leh and Srinagar–Leh roads, among the highest in the world.
Clears the snow off Himalayan passes each spring to reopen them for the summer.
Also builds roads in Bhutan, Afghanistan, Myanmar and other friendly countries.
